question: The average weight of Vipul, Mohan and Mohammad is 45 kg. If the average weight of Vipul and Mohan is 43 kg and that of Mohan and Mohammad is 50 kg, then the weight of Mohan (in kg) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Weight of Mohan = (Sum of first two + Sum of last two) − Sum of all three

Weight of Mohan = (2 × 43 + 2 × 50) − (3 × 45)

Weight of Mohan = (86 + 100) − 135

Weight of Mohan = 186 − 135 = 51

**∴ The correct answer is 51 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of Vipul, Mohan, and Mohammad = 45 kg

Average weight of Vipul and Mohan = 43 kg

Average weight of Mohan and Mohammad = 50 kg

**Formula Used:**

Total Weight = Average Weight × Number of Persons

**Calculation:**

 
 Total = 135 kg
 
 Vipul + Mohan = 86 kg
 
 Mohan + Mohammad = 100 kg
 
• 
 
• 
 Overlap = Mohan
 Mohan = 86 + 100 − 135 = 51 kg

⇒ Total weight of Vipul, Mohan, and Mohammad = 45 × 3 = 135 kg

⇒ Total weight of Vipul and Mohan = 43 × 2 = 86 kg

⇒ Total weight of Mohan and Mohammad = 50 × 2 = 100 kg

⇒ Total of the two pairs = (Vipul + Mohan) + (Mohan + Mohammad) = 86 + 100 = 186 kg

⇒ The sum of the pairs includes Mohan's weight exactly twice.

⇒ Weight of Mohan = Sum of the two pairs − Total weight of all three

⇒ Weight of Mohan = 186 − 135 = 51 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 51 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Average

When two groups of sizes n₁ and n₂ have averages A₁ and A₂ respectively, the combined average is calculated as (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Deviation Method in Averages

The sum of deviations of all observations from their respective average is always zero. This property can be used as a shortcut to quickly find missing variables without large multiplications.

Replacement Method

If a new item replaces an old item and the average increases, the value of the new item is equal to the value of the old item plus the product of total members and the net increase in the average.
